p:cNvPr.descr: Part 2: A diagram that shows the use of pBR322 to clone foreign DNA in E. coli and identify cells containing the DNA. The diagram begins at the top with a group of 7 PBR322 plasmids (labeled left). These are yellow rings with a short green section and a slightly longer blue section, divided by a yellow region. The green region is labeled ampR and the blue region is labeled tetR. Below this image there is a down arrow with blue text to the right reading, “PstI restriction endonuclease” and a gray text box to the left reading, “(1) pBR322 is cleaved in the ampR gene by PstI.” Below the down arrow, the plasmids have pieces of their ampR (green) region removed. To the right are small, complementary curved red fragments labeled “foreign DNA.” Below there is a down arrow with a convergent arrow labeled “DNA ligase” in blue. To the left is a gray text box reading, “(2) DNA fragments to be cloned are ligated to cleaved pBR322. Where ligation is successful, the ampR gene is disrupted. The tetR gene remains intact.” Below the arrow, the cleaved pBR322 plasmids have the red DNA fragments of varying lengths incorporated into their cleavage site, between two green sections of ampR. 2 of the plasmids have no incorporated DNA fragments and are intact. Below is a down arrow with a gray text box to the left reading, (3) E. coli cells are transformed, then grown on agar plates containing tetracycline to select for those that have taken up plasmid.” On the right is text reading, “Transformation of E. coli cells.” Below this arrow is a cluster of 6 E. coli cells, which are bacillus (rod) shaped and off-white. All have a blue tangled string like structure on the left end, which is the genetic material. 2 of the cells have a transformed plasmid inside them, on the far right end. The others are untransformed. Below is a down arrow with text to the right reading, “selection of transformed cells.” Below is an image of a round petri dish, with a dark green agar background and dozens of white dots representing colonies. On the left is text reading, “All colonies have plasmids” and on the right is a label pointing to the dark green agar labeled, “Agar containing tetracycline.” Below this is a down arrow that is split at the lower end. To the right is text reading, “Colonies transferred for testing,” and to the left is a gray text box that reads, “(4) Individual colonies are transferred to matching positions on additional plates. One plate contains tetracycline, the other tetracycline and ampicillin.” Below left side of the split arrow is an image of a petri dish with dark green agar and 6 organized rows of white colonies. Below, the plate is labeled, “Agar containing tetracycline (control).” 6 of the colonies are indicated by a pointer with the label, “Colonies with recombinant plasmids.” Below the right side of the split arrow is a petri dish with dark green agar and 6 rows of irregularly sized colonies, with some so small they are barely visible. Below, the dish is labeled, “Agar containing ampicillin + tetracycline.” Below these images is a gray text box that reads, “(5) Cells that grow on tetracycline but not on tetracycline + ampicillin contain recombinant plasmids with disrupted ampicillin resistance, hence the foreign DNA. Cells with pBR322 without foreign DNA retain ampicillin resistance and grow on both plates.”
